2027-01-23.title: Saturday after the Second Sunday after Denho
readings: The mediator of a better covenant
2027-01-23.alt: Season of Denho. Church Unity Octave. Tomorrow is Kohne Sunday, the commemoration of departed priests.
2027-01-23.verse: But Jesus has now obtained a more excellent ministry, and to that degree he is the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted through better promises.
theo: Hebrews gives us “the main point”: “we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens”. The priests of the old covenant served “a sketch and shadow of the heavenly one”; Jesus serves in the true sanctuary and is “the mediator of a better covenant”. Tomorrow is Kohne Sunday, when our Church prays for its departed priests. Every priest, living or departed, shares in the one priesthood of Christ, and is a weak vessel of his grace.

In the Gospel a mute man, possessed by a demon, is brought to Jesus. When the demon is cast out, “the one who had been mute spoke; and the crowds were amazed.” Christ opens mouths to praise God. Yet the Pharisees say he works by the ruler of demons. The same act brings wonder to some and suspicion to others. Let our mouths, opened by Christ in Baptism, be used for praise and witness, and let us pray tomorrow for the priests who taught us to speak the faith.
outline: Ask: which priest has most helped you in your faith?
Christ opens our mouths for praise.
live: Write down the names of departed priests you knew, to pray for them tomorrow.
Speak one word of faith or praise to someone today.
2027-01-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, our great high priest, mediator of a better covenant, open our lips to praise you. Bless all priests who serve your Church, and grant rest to the priests who have gone before us in faith. Amen.
altar: At the altar the priest stands in the person of Christ, the one high priest, who offers himself in the Holy Qurbono for us.

quick: Jesus is our high priest at God's right hand.
He is the mediator of a better covenant.
He opens the mouths of the mute to praise God.
2027-01-23.action: Write the names of departed priests you knew, to pray for them tomorrow.
2027-01-23.question: Do I use my lips for praise and witness?

family.explain: A man could not speak. Jesus healed him and he began to talk! Jesus helps us to speak kindly and to praise God.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for priests who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we say a thank-you prayer for our parish priest?”

illus: In a parish near Kollam the people still tell of a priest who served them for thirty years and died during an epidemic, visiting the sick. On Kohne Sunday old parishioners light candles at his grave. One said: he taught my whole family to pray; the least I can do is pray for him now.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our high priest, open our lips to praise you and bless your priests. Amen.
share: We have such a high priest (Hebrews 8:1). Do I trust Christ to intercede for me?
A sketch and shadow of the heavenly one (Hebrews 8:5). Do I see the heavenly reality in the liturgy?
The one who had been mute spoke (Matthew 9:33). Where is Christ asking me to speak?
pm.resp: Christ our high priest, hear us.
interc: For our Pope, bishops and priests.
For departed priests, as we prepare for Kohne Sunday.
For those who cannot speak or hear.
pm.close: Father, your Son is our high priest in the heavens. Bless the priests of your Church and open our lips to praise you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us the main point: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens (Hebrews 8:1). He is the mediator of a better covenant (Hebrews 8:6).
The old priesthood was a sketch and shadow; Christ is the reality. Tomorrow, Kohne Sunday, we pray for our departed priests, who shared in Christ's priesthood with all their human weakness.
In the Gospel a mute man is healed and speaks, and the crowds are amazed (Matthew 9:33). Christ opens mouths for praise.
Let us use our lips for praise and witness, and tomorrow let us remember with gratitude the priests who taught us to pray. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus helped a man who could not speak to talk again! Let us use our mouths to say kind words and to praise God.

intro: Theme: “The mediator of a better covenant.”
Christ our high priest, the reality behind every shadow, who opens our lips.

q: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Now the main point in what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
points.apply: Pray tomorrow for departed priests by name.

q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
But Jesus has now obtained a more excellent ministry, and to that degree he is the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted through better promises.
points.apply: Attend the Qurbono tomorrow with awareness of the heavenly liturgy.

q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert;
And when the demon had been cast out, the one who had been mute spoke; and the crowds were amazed and said, “Never has anything like this been seen in Israel.”
points.apply: Speak one word of witness this week.

concl: Christ is our high priest and the reality of every shadow.
He opens our lips; let us praise and pray for his priests.
2027-01-23.resolve: Pray daily for your parish priest.
